climate.source: Latakia monthly normals as published in Wikipedia 'Latakia': sunshine hours (NOAA 1961-1991) and days with precipitation of 1 mm or more (1991-2020 normals, Starlings Roost Weather). sun_frac = sunshine hours / possible daylight hours at 35.5N (day length from the solar declination at mid-month); rain_frac = precipitation days / days in month; temp_c = monthly mean temperature (1991-2020), rounded. wind_ms, wind_from_deg and fog are hand-tuned judgment calls, not measured.
climate.wind_from_source: Judgment call, no table read: the Syrian coast has a west to south-west sea breeze most of the year (west-south-west in summer) and south to south-west winds with the winter storms; the monthly values and the 30 degree scatter are guesses in the style of the Caucasus table, not measurements.

background: Units of Syria's northern coast, calling themselves the Northern Coastal Command (NCC), have refused Damascus's orders and crossed toward the Hatay border. They hold the coast around Latakia and Bassel Al-Assad with the aircraft that came with them: old MiG-21s and MiG-23s, Su-17 strike jets and a few Su-24s, under SA-2 and SA-3 batteries, guns and shoulder-fired missiles. Damascus says it cannot control them; the border commanders say they are protecting Syrian land. Neither is believed.

Turkey has asked for help and a US-led coalition has answered. The carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower and her air wing operate from the eastern Mediterranean; Coalition squadrons fly from Incirlik and the fields behind the Turkish front. You fly with the Navy's carrier air wing or with the Air Force, as your squadron is. The aim is limited: push the NCC back from the border and take Bassel Al-Assad, so a buffer zone opens and the crisis ends in days, not months.
1.intent: Coalition command's intent: keep the NCC's supply and air defences under pressure and support the ground force as it pushes the line back. Bassel Al-Assad is the objective. Hold Hatay on the way. Every day the war is planned and the packages go out. Yours is the one you fly yourself.

now.Offensive: The advance is moving. Our ground force at the front outweighs the NCC's here, and the air campaign is keeping it that way.
now.Consolidating: We hold what we took. The next push waits for the takeover to finish; use the time to hit supply and air defence.
now.Holding: The front is not moving. Close air support and supply strikes decide the next move.
now.Under pressure: The NCC is gaining ground on our side of the line. Hold the sector in front of our airfields.
now.Last stand: The final objective is next. Take Bassel Al-Assad and the crisis is over.
now.Defeat: Hatay has fallen and the Coalition has no foothold left on the front. The campaign is lost.

background: Syria has closed its border with Turkey and moved its army to the Hatay frontier, a province Damascus has never fully given up. The Syrian air force flies from the coast and the central plains with MiG-23s, MiG-25 interceptors and a handful of MiG-29s, under a thick belt of SA-2, SA-3 and SA-6 batteries and a few newer SA-11s fitted by Russian advisers. Its supplies come down the coast road from Latakia and the Homs gap, and no one outside Damascus can say who is paying for the new equipment.

A US-led coalition has answered Turkey's request for help. The carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower and her air wing operate from the eastern Mediterranean; Coalition squadrons fly from Incirlik and the Turkish fields behind the front. You fly with the Navy's carrier air wing or with the Air Force, as your squadron is. The war opened at midnight, when F-117A Nighthawks took out the long-range SA-5 batteries near Homs and Damascus. They will be rebuilt in time, but for now the way is open.
2.intent: Coalition command's intent: break Syria's supply and air defence, not its cities. Hit the depots, fuel and the SAM belt along the coast road, and the front cannot be kept up. Hold Hatay, it is the line. Every day the war is planned and the packages go out. Yours is the one you fly yourself.

now.Under pressure: Syria is gaining ground toward Hatay. Hold the sector in front of our airfields.
now.Last stand: Hatay is the line. If it falls, the war is lost.
now.Defeat: Hatay has fallen and the Coalition has no foothold left on the front. The campaign is lost.

background: Syria has closed its border with Turkey and is massing along the Hatay frontier, backed by Russian advisers, Russian-supplied fighters and a modern air-defence network that Syria could never have paid for. Behind it stands one man. Aleksandr Lutorin, a Russian oligarch whose companies hold the pipelines, terminals and tanker fleets that carry the Levant's oil and gas to the Mediterranean, has bought his way into both governments. Damascus takes his money; Moscow takes his calls. Hatay and the Iskenderun coast are the last piece of the export route he does not control.

A US-led coalition has answered Turkey's request for help. The carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower and her air wing operate from the eastern Mediterranean; Coalition squadrons fly from Incirlik and the fields behind the Turkish front. You fly with the Navy's carrier air wing or with the Air Force, as your squadron is. The war opened at midnight, when F-117A Nighthawks slipped in unseen and took out the long-range SA-5 batteries around Damascus and Homs. The rest of the network, and the Russian-built fighters behind it, are still up.
3.intent: Coalition command's intent: break Syria's supply and air defence, not its cities. Take down the SAM belt, the fuel and the depots that feed the front, and the war is over when the enemy can no longer keep it up. Hold Hatay: it is the line. Every day the war is planned and the packages go out. Yours is the one you fly yourself.

now.Under pressure: Syrian-Russian forces are gaining ground toward Hatay. Hold the sector in front of our airfields.
now.Last stand: Hatay is the line. If it falls, the war is lost.
now.Defeat: Hatay has fallen and the Coalition has no foothold left on the front. The campaign is lost.
